summary: Ten comment-endorsed networking, wildlife, art, learning, and workflow picks from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Bitbang
items.source_story_title: Internet centralization and the original sin of NAT
items.summary: A CLI for direct peer-to-peer file transfer through NAT and firewalls.
items.why_included: A user recommended it from experience and highlighted a workable free TURN allowance.
items.evidence: The commenter invited readers to try Bitbang, said they use it, and saw clear potential.

evidence_sources.author: CrimsonCape
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using it and it certainly has the potential.

items.name: Warrant
items.source_story_title: Agent memory as a file format
items.summary: A Markdown verification tool that keeps agent documentation checked and current.
items.why_included: Its creator described a concrete handoff workflow that re-verifies facts between agent sessions.
items.evidence: The creator uses Warrant to embed rerunnable checks and force documentation verification during handoffs.

evidence_sources.author: pwython
evidence_sources.excerpt: It keeps documentation from going out of date by embedding re-runnable verification checks directly inside markdown files (that the agents use, not humans).

items.name: Links
items.source_story_title: P99 0 ms* autocomplete for 240M domain names
items.summary: A lightweight text and graphics web browser with no JavaScript engine.
items.why_included: A three-decade text-browser user strongly preferred Links over Lynx and uses it daily.
items.evidence: The commenter called Links their preferred daily text browser and uses it for local HTML every day.

evidence_sources.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
evidence_sources.excerpt: One of the many reasons I prefer links (no graphics) I use links as an offline HTML reader; I am opening local HTML files every day

items.name: BirdNET-Go
items.source_story_title: I turned my security cameras into an automatic bird identification system
items.summary: A self-hosted wildlife sound analyzer for continuous local species identification.
items.why_included: A Home Assistant user reported a successful multi-camera GPU setup for birds and frogs.
items.evidence: The commenter runs BirdNET-Go with three RTSP streams and said the setup works swimmingly.

evidence_sources.author: inventor7777
evidence_sources.excerpt: I run BirdNET-Go as an app on my Home Assistant i7 M710q. I use the GPU-enabled BirdNET model and Perch V2, and it works swimmingly.

items.name: Merlin Bird ID
items.source_story_title: I turned my security cameras into an automatic bird identification system
items.summary: Cornell's free app for identifying birds by sound, photo, or description.
items.why_included: A frequent user reported good results across multiple countries.
items.evidence: The commenter uses Merlin Bird ID all the time and found it reliable internationally.

evidence_sources.author: bakibab
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Merlin Bird ID all the time. I found it good across many countries.

items.name: Futel
items.summary: A free public-phone network combining useful calls with interactive urban art.
items.why_included: A commenter highlighted Futel among the neat public payphone art projects.
items.evidence: The commenter praised public payphone art and singled out Futel's elaborate menus and installations.

evidence_sources.author: NelsonMinar
evidence_sources.excerpt: There's a bunch of neat public payphone art projects out there. A friend of mine runs Futel, which has some fairly elaborate voice menus and several phones installed.

items.name: Mouseland
items.summary: Maggie Rudy's handcrafted miniature mouse world, characters, props, and photo stories.
items.why_included: A commenter called Rudy one of the most impressive miniature artists they had seen.
items.evidence: The commenter strongly praised the artist and highlighted the storytelling within each photograph.

evidence_sources.author: skybrian

items.name: SIMI Studio
items.summary: A video channel featuring animated miniature scenes starring a hamster.
items.why_included: A commenter fondly recalled watching the channel extensively during COVID.
items.evidence: The commenter said they watched SIMI Studio a lot and described its miniature hamster animations.

evidence_sources.author: Otterly99
evidence_sources.excerpt: This reminds me of this youtube channel[1] that I used to watch a lot during COVID where the author animates miniature scenes with their hamster.
